item.title: Electro magnetism
item.description:
Light

स्फटिकाद्य्-अन्तरितोपलब्धिर् अपि
प्रसाद-स्वभावतया स्फटिकादीनां तेजोगतेर् अ-प्रतिबन्धकतया
प्रदीप-प्रभेवोपपन्नेति।

  • उदयनः, किरणावली, तेजःप्रकरणम्

“The reason why one can see through crystal & so forth is because these substances have prasāda (transparency/purity), due to which they do not hinder the movement of light (passing through them).”

  • Udayana (~10th century CE), Kiraṇāvalī

Magnetism

Bhāsarvajña (~10th century CE) imagined that a magnet changes the vāyu (loosely translated as ‘air’) around itself due to which the air also acts like a magnet and attracts the things which are within its purview.

item.title: Magnetic field
item.description:
Source: TW

Ancient Indians Discussing Magnetic Field

In Tattvasaṅgraha, Śāntarakṣita quotes mata of a (sambhavataḥ tīrthika) saiddhāntika ācārya named Śaṅkarasvāmi and dismisses it. Śaṅkarasvāmi’s mata has aucitya for vartamānaloka, who have been avagata with sāmānyasiddhānta-s of bhautikī (physics). Mūḍha-s are those who say, out of their ajñātā & vismṛti, that the mata of ayaskāntīyakṣetra (magnetic field) didn’t exist among ārya-s before the vāda-s of Faraday, Ørsted, etc. gained prasiddhi. Although not all saiddhāntika-s did grahaṇa of such a mata due to dārśanika bheda-s, it was prajñāta among budha-s in a non-mathematical vikasita rūpa.
